chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Harun ibn Muslim the scribe who used to narrate in Sarr al-Manna, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abdul Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding His saying, Exalted is He:
Or, who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil, and makes you successors in the earth? [Is] there a deity with Allah? Little do you remember. {62}

He said: This verse was revealed regarding al-Qa'im (the Awaited Imam). Gabriel (peace be upon him) was on the drainspout in the form of a white bird, and he will be the first of God's creation to pay allegiance to him (I mean Gabriel). Then the people will pay allegiance to him, three hundred and thirteen. Whoever is tested with walking will arrive at that hour, and whoever is not tested with walking will disappear from his bed. This is the saying of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him): 'The missing ones are from their beds.' And it is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'For each is a direction towards which he turns; so compete in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.' {148} He said: The good deeds are the Wilayah (guardianship) for us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Qa'im' referred to in the interpretation of Quran 2:163 and how do the companions join him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* offers a distinct Shia eschatological interpretation of Quran 2:163, identifying the 'distressed one' (al-Mudtir) and 'successors in the earth' (Khalifa) specifically as al-Qa'im, the Twelfth Imam. It elaborates on the miraculous nature of his emergence, noting that Gabriel pledges allegiance first, followed by 313 companions, while those unable to travel are miraculously transported from their beds—a phenomenon linked to the concept of *Ghaybat al-Kubra*. Furthermore, it contextualizes the 'racing in good deeds' from Quran 2:148 as the pursuit of *Wilayah* (authority) of the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the theological centrality of the Imams in Shia soteriology.
